title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, following the previous and next pages of the 'Longue Marche' continuation (ms. p. 709). X is a space (or curve) with base point x0 and π = π1(X,x0). A group Γ (e.g. an arithmetic Galois group) acts on X. M is the structure group of the coverings considered, and on this page it is effectively abelian; the previous page has M-torsors obtained from X̃/[π,π], so M is probably π^ab or a quotient of it. M̃ is an extension 1 → M → M̃ → Γ → 1 that arises from the extension of Γ by π after pushing out along π → M. Γ acts on M by conjugation inside M̃; write γ_M for the action of γ.

The crossed-out text at the top introduces θ0, the 'canonical' action of 𝔊 = M/[Π,Π] on X'_0 = X̃/[Π,Π], and an arbitrary action θ satisfying the same conditions. Grothendieck abandons this and reformulates.

Problem. Let X' → X be a covering. It is described by its fibre E at x0, which is an M-torsor, with π acting on E by translations through π → M. We want X' to be a covering of the pair (X, Γ-action), i.e. we want the Γ-action on X to lift to X'. In fibre terms: extend the given action on E (of π, factoring through M-translations) to an action of M̃ on E. That action restricts on M ⊂ M̃ to the torsor translations.

Claim (formula 280). Any such action is by affine transformations of the torsor E. For g ∈ M̃ over γ ∈ Γ, λ ∈ M and x ∈ E:
  g(λ·x) = γ_M(λ)·(g x).
Proof: g(λx) = (gλ)x = (gλg⁻¹g)x = (gλg⁻¹)(gx), and gλg⁻¹ = γ_M(λ).

Next page. The lifted action is the same thing as a homomorphism M̃ → Aff(E) into the affine group of the torsor. Here Aff(E) ≅ M ⋊ Aut(M), the holomorph, once a point of E is chosen. The homomorphism must make a morphism of extensions
  (1 → M → M̃ → Γ → 1) → (1 → M → Aff(E) → Aut(M) → 1),
with identity on M and the given map Γ → Aut(M). So the category of the sought liftings X' is equivalent to the category of pairs (E, θ). The standard consequence for abelian M is:
- a lift exists iff the class of M̃ in H²(Γ, M) vanishes, since Aff(E) pulled back to Γ is the split extension M ⋊ Γ;
- the lifts then form a torsor under H¹(Γ, M);
- equivalently, lifts correspond to splittings of M̃ → Γ, up to the choice of a point of E.
This is the abelianised (π^ab) layer of the section-conjecture problem: Γ-equivariant π^ab-torsors versus sections of the abelianised fundamental extension, i.e. Albanese-torsor-type obstructions.
errors: The exact sequence 1 → M → Aff(E) → Aut(M) → 1, with M embedded by translations and composite M → Aut(M) trivial, is only correct for abelian M. For non-abelian M, a left translation by μ sends λ ↦ μλμ⁻¹ in formula (280), so M maps onto Inn(M), not trivially. One would then need Out(M), or the kernel would be the twisted group of torsor automorphisms. The page implicitly assumes M abelian (consistent with M = π^ab from the previous page), but does not say so.
Formula (280) holds only if the M̃-action on E restricts on M to the given torsor action. This is part of the intended conditions but is not stated on the page.

There is notational drift: the text says 'action de M sur E qui se factorisera par M̃', where the intended meaning is an action of the extension M̃, compatible with M-translations. It also writes 'revêtement de (X', …)' where it means a covering of the pair (X, Γ).

ideas.what: A lift of a Γ-action from X to a covering X' (fibre E, an M-torsor) amounts to extending the π-action on E to an action of the extension M̃ of Γ by M.
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant structures on coverings / extension of the fundamental-group action to the arithmetic fundamental group
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental group, exact homotopy sequence); La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Such an action is necessarily affine on the torsor: g(λx) = γ_M(λ)·gx, with a one-line proof.
ideas.modern_name: Holomorph / affine group of a torsor, semilinear automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group theory; Giraud's non-abelian cohomology for the torsor formulation
ideas.where_published: Analogous formalism in SGA1 Exp. XIII and in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne; not this exact formula

ideas.what: Classification of liftings as morphisms of extensions into 1 → M → Aff(E) → Aut(M) → 1, leading (next page) to an obstruction in H²(Γ,M) and a torsor under H¹(Γ,M).
ideas.modern_name: Obstruction theory for group extensions / abelianised section-conjecture (π^ab) layer
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–MacLane (extensions); for the anabelian setting, later work on the abelian / 2-nilpotent section conjecture (Wickelgren, Esnault–Wittenberg and others)
ideas.where_published: Ideas of this kind appear in the 1983 letter to Faltings and in the Longue Marche; this precise formulation is not known to be published

deep.surprise_reason: The page carries out a routine and correct computation: lifting a Γ-action to a π^ab-type torsor covering forces affine actions, giving a morphism of extensions into the holomorph. This is standard group-extension and torsor theory. It belongs to Grothendieck's abelianised approach to the section problem, which later work has treated independently. Nothing here is new to a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Under formula (280) the labels are: g ∈ M̃ (with a crossed-out symbol), λ ∈ M (not M̃), x ∈ E.
The '$' in 'se fera nécessairement [?] $ [?]' is a stray mark; the sense is 'cette action se fera nécessairement à travers le groupe affine du torseur'.
'g ∈ M̃ au-dessus de γ ∈ Γ': the image reads 'g ∈ M̃ — au-dessus de γ ∈ Γ' with a crossed-out letter before M̃.
'pour x ∈ E, λ ∈ M' is preceded by '— on aura alors' ('on aura donc' is possible); the transcription is acceptable.
'(X', [?])' is probably intended as a covering of '(X, Γ)', i.e. of X with its Γ-action; the symbol after the comma is heavily overwritten.
